newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee mixed in dull midday trade, off lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee mixed in dull midday trade, off lows.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures recovered from early weakness and traded mixed ahead of midday, buoyed by local short-covering, dealers said.

Spot September arabicas were up 0.05 cent per lb as of 1149 EDT, to 178.00 cents, after ranging between 179.50 and 175.00 cents. Most-active December fell 1.10 cents, to 160.75 cents, after ranging from 162.00 and 158.50. The back months were down 2.20 to up 0.40.
Coffee prices headed lower at the outset, defying an up 1.00-cent pre-opening call, as commission houses sold after a rise in U.S. warehouse inventories during July, traders said.
Supplies of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses rose in July by 219,000 60-kg bags, to 2,335,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported after Friday's close.
"GCA was neutral to slightly bearish," said one dealer. "It was about 50,000 more than people had anticipated, but a stock increase was already priced in."

With September going into delivery period on Thursday, traders expect liquidation and rolling forward of the spot contract to keep some pressure on the market. As of Friday, September open interest stood at 5,372 lots, down 441 lots from the previous session.
"There's still a lot to be done in the next three days," said a trader.
Technically, traders pegged September support at 175.00 cents, followed by 172.50-172.00 cents. On the upside, resistance was seen at 180.00, with buy-stops said to be building above 181.00 cents.
Volume as of 1100 EDT was light, at an estimated 2,928 lots.
